errors.english: such as existence and the like
errors.why: The side opens mid-word continuing མི་རྟག་ from the previous side: the shared property is impermanence (anityatva), not existence.

fix.find: such as existence and the like
fix.replace: such as impermanence and the like

errors.english: Regarding "Similar distinctions in the case of similar properties,"
errors.why: The Tibetan cites the verse words following vikalpasama (the named jāti) — 'a difference is stated even for similarity' — and the English mangles the jāti name into the quoted phrase.

errors.english: is shown to have multiple meanings; here, the action should be understood
errors.why: It is the verb 'making' (byed pa, kṛ) that has many meanings and here means 'entailing', not the whole phrase 'will absurdly follow as undifferentiated'.

note: Follows the argument on aviśeṣasama reasonably, but misreads the opening property and blurs two grammatical/jāti points.

errors.english: All parts of the syllogism exist for the sake of the relationship between what is to be proven and the means of proof.
errors.why: The point is that every member of the argument proves the probandum, so 'proving the sādhya' cannot single out the reason; the English loses that.

note: A sound rendering of the grammatical discussion of the ablative in udāharaṇasādharmyāt; one reason clause is blurred.

errors.english: just as commanded by the divine order
errors.why: In the drama ལྷ (deva) is the form of address for the king, 'Your/His Majesty', not a divine command.

fix.find: just as commanded by the divine order

note: Lively and faithful rendering of the drama scene; one stage-direction honorific misread.
Faithful rendering of the Madhyamaka verses, citations (Yuktiṣaṣṭikā, MMK, Āryadeva, Prajñāpāramitā, Kāśyapaparivarta) and the Cārvāka verse.

errors.english: at that time it is the (Tathagata) the One Thus Gone; a Buddha
errors.why: The verse says that then all (beings) would be Tathāgatas, a reductio, not that the mind is the Tathāgata.

fix.find: at that time it is the (Tathagata) the One Thus Gone; a Buddha
fix.replace: at that time all beings are (Tathagata) Ones Thus Gone; Buddhas

note: Bodhicaryāvatāra IX verses rendered accurately in content, though as prose rather than verse; one reductio misread.
Faithful verse rendering of the sūtra citations and the Lotus Sūtra passage; a few loose but defensible readings.

errors.english: This rule does apply to all categories of downfalls such as theft
errors.why: The Tibetan says this rule is NOT applied to all classes of offence such as theft, only to killing.

fix.find: This rule does apply to all categories of downfalls such as theft
fix.replace: This rule does not apply to all categories of downfalls such as theft

errors.english: (payantika) an offense requiring confession and forfeiture
errors.why: ལྟུང་བྱེད (pāyattika) is a simple expiatory offence; forfeiture belongs to naiḥsargika-pāyattika (spang ltung).

fix.find: (payantika) an offense requiring confession and forfeiture
fix.replace: (payantika) an offense requiring expiation through confession

errors.english: regarding those non-humans and animals who belong to the human realm or take on the physical forms of others
errors.why: The being is one belonging to the human realm who displays the bodily form of the non-human and animal realms, not non-humans and animals belonging to the human realm.

note: Generally follows the Vinaya casuistry on killing/stealing across realms, but inverts the key restriction to killing and mis-glosses pāyattika.
Accurate rendering of the Ratnakūṭa, Sarvāstivāda Vinaya, Mañjuśrīvikrīḍita and Gaṇḍavyūha citations.
Faithful rendering of Vigrahavyāvartanī verses 30–33 and the autocommentary, with correct pramāṇa terminology.

errors.english: challenges whether the primary definition [note: referring to literal or primary meaning] is exclusively that which has a non-existent entity as its object
errors.why: The objection proposes that having a non-existent object is precisely the defining mark of the non-primary (gauṇa, figurative), not of the primary.

fix.find: challenges whether the primary definition [note: referring to literal or primary meaning] is exclusively that which has a non-existent entity as its object
fix.replace: proposes that having a non-existent entity as its object is precisely the defining mark of the secondary [note: gauṇa, figurative usage]

errors.english: Because the Nihilist [note: literally: "one who speaks of non-existence"] speaks of non-existence, "non-existence" is expressed; this refers to the listener [note: or "auditor" of the doctrine] regarding the Pradhana
errors.why: No nihilist and no listener: 'expressing the non-existent' describes the words (མཉན་པ, śruti) for pradhāna etc., which denote non-existent things.

fix.find: Because the Nihilist [note: literally: "one who speaks of non-existence"] speaks of non-existence, "non-existence" is expressed; this refers to the listener [note: or "auditor" of the doctrine] regarding the Pradhana
fix.replace: Because it speaks of the non-existent it "expresses the non-existent": this refers to the words (śruti) for the Pradhana

errors.english: According to your desire [note: addressing the opponent], the Pradhana and such are not actual entities
errors.why: The pradhāna etc. are what the opponent accepts; that they are not entities is the author's claim, not the opponent's.

fix.find: According to your desire [note: addressing the opponent], the Pradhana and such are not actual entities
fix.replace: The Pradhana and such that you accept [note: addressing the opponent] are not actual entities

errors.why: མཉན་པ here is the word (śruti) that expresses the non-existent, not a listener.

fix.replace: That word which expresses the non-existent

errors.english: the unsuitability of manifold effects is admitted
errors.why: The Tibetan says the capacity (suitability) for many effects is accepted.

fix.find: the unsuitability of manifold effects is admitted
fix.replace: the capacity for manifold effects is admitted

errors.english: one still listens to the teachings on the Pradhana and so forth
errors.why: The construction is 'just as the words for pradhāna etc. are used', again śruti as word, not listening to teachings.

fix.find: one still listens to the teachings on the Pradhana and so forth
fix.replace: the words for the Pradhana and so forth are still used

errors.english: that which has an entity as its object is also seen directly
errors.why: དངོས་སུ here means 'as primary/literal' (mukhya) in the gauṇa/mukhya discussion, not 'seen directly'.

errors.english: meaning the Pradhana and so forth are reduced to ashes
errors.why: ཐལ་བ continues onto the next side (ཐལ་བ་དག་གི་བཟློག་པ) and means consequences (prasaṅga), not ashes.

note: The gauṇa/mukhya argument against Sāṃkhya terms is systematically misread (śruti taken as 'listener', primary/secondary inverted, opponent's view misattributed).
